paper.title: TAS1R3 biases bone marrow stromal cell fate toward adipogenesis through PLCβ4-p38 signaling.
paper.abstract: How mesenchymal lineage allocation is regulated by nutrients remains poorly understood. Here, we identify TAS1R3, which has been recognized as a component of taste receptors in the taste buds, as being expressed in bone marrow stromal cells (BMSCs) and as a regulator of BMSC fate. Genetic deletion or pharmacological inhibition of TAS1R3 impaired adipogenic differentiation in primary BMSCs, whereas TAS1R3 overexpression enhanced adipogenesis in a BMSC-derived cell line. Consistent results were observed in a human MSC model, in which TAS1R3 promoted adipogenic differentiation and suppressed osteogenic differentiation. Transcriptomic, pharmacological, and knockdown analyses showed that TAS1R3 promotes adipogenesis through phospholipase C beta 4 (PLCβ4)-dependent p38 mitogen-activated protein kinase (MAPK) activation. In contrast, under osteogenic conditions, TAS1R3 attenuated p38 phosphorylation, reduced alkaline phosphatase activity, and restrained osteogenic differentiation. Together, these findings identify TAS1R3 as a context-dependent regulator of p38 signaling and show that extraoral TAS1R3 signaling directs mesenchymal lineage allocation toward adipogenesis at the expense of osteogenesis.

paper.title: Ocean Acidification Impairs Olfaction in the Large Yellow Croaker, Larimichthys crocea, by Disrupting Sensory Integrity and Neural Processing.
paper.abstract: Ocean acidification (OA) poses a significant threat to marine organisms, yet its effects on fish sensory systems remain poorly understood. This study investigated the effects of elevated pCO2 on olfactory function in the large yellow croaker, Larimichthys crocea. Elevated pCO2 reduced peripheral olfactory sensitivity, as evidenced by suppressed electro-olfactogram responses. This impairment was accompanied by epithelial disorganization, cellular damage, increased apoptosis in the olfactory epithelium, and reduced expression of olfactory neuron markers. In vitro analyses using a selected recombinant L. crocea odorant receptor LORA1-1 showed that acidified pH altered its physicochemical properties and odorant-specific receptor-ligand interaction dynamics. OA also downregulated genes associated with odorant receptor expression, G protein-mediated signaling, calcium-related transduction, and neuronal maturation. Telencephalic responses included altered ion-transport ATPase activities, histopathological abnormalities, oxidative stress, enhanced apoptotic activity, and reduced neuropeptide Y expression. Transcriptomic and proteomic analyses further identified telencephalic molecular changes associated with altered neuroactive ligand-receptor interaction, calcium signaling, glutathione metabolism, apoptosis, mitophagy, MAPK signaling, and olfactory transduction. Our findings suggest that epithelial injury, altered odorant recognition, and disrupted peripheral signaling contribute to OA-induced olfactory impairment in L. crocea, with potential consequences for migration and reproduction that depend on olfactory cues.

paper.title: A glutamatergic circuit from the piriform cortex to the mediodorsal thalamus regulates trigeminal neuropathic pain and comorbid cognitive impairment in mice.
paper.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Trigeminal neuropathic pain (TNP) is a chronic, debilitating pain disorder affecting the orofacial region. Patients often experience concomitant cognitive impairment, severely impacting their quality of life. The principal neural circuit mechanisms that link TNP to cognitive dysfunction remain unclear. The piriform cortex (PIR), primarily recognised for its role in olfaction, has not been systematically investigated in trigeminal neuropathic pain processing or pain-related cognitive dysfunction.

METHODS: This study utilised pseudorabies virus-mediated multisynaptic retrograde tracing to map whole-brain anatomical connectivity associated with orofacial sensory pathways. c-Fos immunofluorescence staining and in vivo fibre-optic calcium signalling recordings were used to detect alterations in glutamatergic neuronal activity within the PIR of TNP model mice. Chemogenetic and optogenetic techniques were employed to manipulate PIR glutamatergic (PIRGlu) neurons in a bidirectional manner, validating their functional roles in pain and cognitive regulation. Anterograde viral tracing was integrated with circuit-specific chemogenetic intervention to elucidate downstream regulatory pathways.

RESULTS: This study identified the PIR as a previously unrecognized brain region anatomically associated with trigeminal neuropathic pain-related pathways, providing evidence for its potential involvement in TNP. PIRGlu neurons in TNP model mice exhibited marked burst-like activation, with in vivo calcium activity intensity exhibiting considerable synchronisation with facial pain-sensitive behaviour. Chemogenetic inhibition of PIRGlu neurons significantly increased pain thresholds and ameliorated cognitive deficits in TNP mice, whereas selective activation of PIRGlu neurons in sham mice recapitulated the pain-cognition comorbidity phenotype, demonstrating the essential role of these neurons in mediating pain-related cognitive dysfunction. Viral tracing identified the mediodorsal thalamus (MD) as a critical downstream target of PIRGlu neurons. Electrophysiological recordings further confirmed that PIRGlu neurons establish direct excitatory monosynaptic connections with MD neurons, with fast glutamatergic transmission predominantly mediated by AMPA receptor-dependent signalling. Specific disruption of the PIRGlu-MD circuit simultaneously alleviated pain and cognitive impairment in model mice, while inhibition of PIRGlu neurons markedly reduced calcium activity in downstream MD neurons.

CONCLUSION: This study highlights the PIRGlu-MD circuit as an important pathway contributing to TNP-cognitive impairment comorbidity. Furthermore, it augments our understanding of the non-olfactory physiological functions of the PIR, offering a novel potential target for investigating the mechanisms underlying the association of chronic pain with cognitive impairment.

paper.title: Beyond basic taste: mechanisms, measurement, and food-matrix translation of non-basic oral sensations.
paper.abstract: The five basic tastes-sweet, sour, salty, bitter and umami-account for only part of food acceptance and quality. Non-basic oral sensations, including astringency, pungency, cooling, metallic sensation, fatty mouthfeel, oleogustus, tingling, numbing and kokumi, contribute substantially to hedonic and textural perception and are commercially important, yet remain less well characterized. This integrative critical review synthesizes mechanistic, neurophysiological, analytical and applied evidence for these nine sensations, treating pungency as two mechanistically distinct pathways, TRPV1- and TRPA1-mediated, to give ten mechanistic entries. Each entry is assessed on two distinct axes: mechanistic confidence, how strongly the principal proximal mechanism is supported by available evidence, and food-matrix translation confidence, how reliably that mechanism predicts perception in real foods. The two axes are related but not equivalent: higher confidence in the principal proximal mechanism does not by itself ensure high confidence in food-matrix translation. TRPV1-mediated pungency, TRPM8-mediated cooling, astringency and fatty mouthfeel rest on well-supported principal or proximal mechanisms, yet none of the ten entries reaches high translation confidence, while TRPA1-mediated pungency, tingling, numbing, oleogustus and kokumi are weaker on both axes. Three distinctions are emphasized: pungency is not a single mechanism; fatty mouthfeel is lubrication-based and mechanoreceptor-mediated, whereas oleogustus is a proposed fatty-acid-receptor perception that remains debated; and iron-related metallic sensation arises largely from retronasal perception of lipid-oxidation volatiles, with no specific human metallic receptor identified. The principal conclusion is that a well-supported mechanism does not by itself confer predictive power in food: matrix composition, salivary dilution and oral processing reshape perception, so dynamic and tribological methods are more ecologically valid than static intensity ratings, and these sensations warrant greater consideration in product formulation and sensory evaluation.

paper.title: Localized SARS-CoV-2 Infection Triggers a Tissue-Wide Antiviral Response and Functional Impairment of Olfactory Sensory Neurons.
paper.abstract: Olfactory dysfunction is a hallmark of COVID-19, yet the mechanisms by which severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) infection causes widespread sensory impairment remain incompletely understood. We compared the olfactory epithelial tropism of multiple SARS-CoV-2 variants in a mouse model and observed that Alpha and Beta variants exhibited the greatest infectivity for the olfactory epithelium (OE), whereas Omicron rarely infected this tissue despite comparable pulmonary viral titers. We further defined the effects of SARS-CoV-2 on olfactory sensory neurons (OSNs) using immunohistochemistry, single-cell RNA sequencing, spatial gene expression characterization, and functional odor stimulation. The localized infection of sustentacular cells triggered a tissue-wide interferon-stimulated antiviral response that extended beyond infected regions for Alpha and Beta but was largely absent following Omicron infection. Mature OSNs transiently adopted an interferon-responsive state before exhibiting persistent downregulation of odorant signal transduction, mitochondrial, and activity-dependent gene pathways. Consistent with these transcriptional changes, odor stimulation failed to elicit normal activity-dependent gene expression during SARS-CoV-2 infection, indicating impaired neuronal function without widespread neuronal loss. Progressive accumulation of macrophages further indicated sustained inflammatory remodeling of the OE. Together, these findings demonstrate that SARS-CoV-2 infection initiates tissue-wide antiviral signaling in the OE that persistently disrupts OSN function, providing a mechanistic framework for COVID-19-associated anosmia.

paper.title: Qi Yin San Liang San prevents gefitinib-induced nociceptive hypersensitivity by modulating TRPV1 channel activity.
paper.abstract:
ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Qi Yin San Liang San (QYSLS) is a traditional Chinese medicine formula used as an adjunctive therapy for malignant tumors, and has been reported to reduce treatment-related toxicities. Gefitinib-associated nociceptive hypersensitivity remains underrecognized, with its underlying causal mechanism poorly defined. It is unclear whether QYSLS can prevent gefitinib-evoked adverse effect and the underlying molecular mechanism remain unknown.

AIM OF THE STUDY: To explore the molecular mechanism of gefitinib-provoked nociceptive hypersensitivity and evaluate the preventive effects of QYSLS, with specific investigation of TRPV1 channel activity and CGRP release from dorsal root ganglion (DRG) neuron under this pathological condition.

METHODS: A mouse model of gefitinib-provoked nociceptive hypersensitivity was established. QYSLS protection was assessed via pain behavioral tests and DRG histopathology. RNA-seq and network pharmacology were used for target screening. Surface plasmon resonance (SPR), cellular thermal shift assay (CETSA) and molecular docking confirmed direct gefitinib-TRPV1 binding. Calcium imaging evaluated TRPV1 channel activity in primary DRG neurons and TRPV1-overexpressing cells. Trpv1-/- mice were used to validate its function. RT-qPCR, immunofluorescence staining and ELISA measured DRG TRPV1/CGRP expression and CGRP release.

RESULTS: Gefitinib induced time-dependent declines in mechanical withdrawal thresholds (8.7% of the control at day 28) and thermal withdrawal latencies (55.3% of control at day 28), accompanied by DRG injury in mice. DRG RNA-seq revealed elevated Trpv1 transcripts levels and enrichment of ion channel pathways. Gefitinib triggered TRPV1-dependent elevation of intracellular Ca2+ signals in DRG nociceptive neurons. Calcium imaging, SPR, CETSA, molecular docking and site-directed mutagenesis showed that gefitinib directly activates TRPV1. Residue Y454 is critical for this effect, while it is dispensable for capsaicin-mediated TRPV1 activation, and this activation elicits significant Ca2+ influx, neuronal excitation, and increased CGRP in DRG neurons. Genetic deletion of Trpv1 largely restored pain thresholds and rescued gefitinib-caused neuropathic pain. Oral QYSLS alleviated gefitinib-evoked weight loss, DRG histological damage and nociceptive hypersensitivity (recovered to 50.5% of control for mechanical withdrawal thresholds, and 94.7% of control for thermal withdrawal latency at day 28), accompanied by reductions in gefitinib-triggered DRG TRPV1 and CGRP expression of ∼34.6% and ∼56.1%, respectively. Quercetin and ferulic acid, the key bioactive ingredients of QYSLS, can inhibit gefitinib-induced TRPV1 activation. The analgesic-protective effects of QYSLS were substantially blunted in Trpv1-/- mice.

CONCLUSIONS: This work identifies a previously unrecognized mechanism: Gefitinib triggers nociceptive hypersensitivity via DRG TRPV1 direct activation. Residue Y454 is critical for gefitinib- but not capsaicin-evoked TRPV1 activation, and CGRP may act as a downstream effector. QYSLS prevents this nociceptive hypersensitivity largely through TRPV1.

paper.title: Staphylococcus aureus-derived xanthine exacerbates allergic rhinitis-induced olfactory dysfunction through promoting Th17 cell differentiation and IL-17A production.
paper.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Allergic rhinitis (AR) is frequently accompanied by olfactory dysfunction (OD), yet the role of microbial metabolites in this process remains poorly elucidated. This study aimed to investigate how xanthine, a metabolite derived from Staphylococcus aureus (Sa), exacerbates AR-induced OD by promoting Th17 cell differentiation and IL-17A production.

METHODS: Multi-omics analyses, comprising metabolomics, proteomics and 16S rRNA gene sequencing, were performed on AR patients and mouse models with AR. Sa was cultured and key metabolites in its supernatant were detected using untargeted metabolomics. AR mice were nasally challenged with Sa supernatant or xanthine, and comparisons were made with mice with chronic AR and OD. The therapeutic potential of an anti-IL-17A neutralising antibody was assessed in AR mice stimulated with Sa supernatant or xanthine.

RESULTS: Purine metabolism was significantly enriched, and xanthine levels were elevated in AR patients and mouse models, particularly those with OD. Airway microbial dysbiosis in AR mice was characterised by increased Staphylococcus abundance, and the Sa infection pathway was enriched in patients with AR. Untargeted metabolomics of Sa supernatant revealed increased xanthine levels and enrichment of purine metabolism. Nasal challenge with Sa supernatant or xanthine significantly exacerbated OD. Mechanistically, xanthine promoted Th17 cell differentiation and IL-17A production. Notably, IL-17A neutralisation effectively alleviated xanthine-exacerbated OD, indicating a pivotal role for the IL-17A pathway in this process.

CONCLUSION: Sa-derived xanthine aggravates AR-induced OD by driving Th17 cell differentiation and IL-17A production. These findings highlight the xanthine-IL-17A pathway as a potential therapeutic target for improving olfactory function in AR.

paper.title: [Progress in research on olfactory dysfunction in patients with obstructive sleep apnea].
paper.abstract: Obstructive sleep apnea （OSA） is a common sleep-related breathing disorder characterized by recurrent upper-airway collapse and intermittent hypoxia, which has been widely recognized for its detrimental effects on neurocognitive function and multiple physiological systems. Emerging evidence indicates that olfactory dysfunction （OD） may represent an important yet long-overlooked manifestation in patients with OSA. Numerous clinical studies have demonstrated that olfactory threshold, discrimination, and identification abilities are significantly impaired in individuals with OSA compared with healthy controls, and the severity of olfactory deficits shows a clear negative correlation with the apnea-hypopnea index. The underlying mechanisms appear to be multifactorial:①damage to the cholinergic neurotransmitter system and cognitive impairment induced by intermittent hypoxia and sleep fragmentation;②structural and functional alterations in brain regions involved in olfactory processing, including the prefrontal cortex, hippocampus, and thalamus;③the impact of elevated body mass index and chronic inflammatory responses on the olfactory epithelium and central olfactory pathways. Continuous positive airway pressure （CPAP）, the first-line therapy for OSA, may partially improve olfactory performance by enhancing ventilation, reducing hypoxemia, and alleviating airway inflammation, although current evidence remains limited by sample size and follow-up duration. Beyond standard OSA management, olfactory training, neurophysiological assessment, and inflammation-modulating interventions may serve as promising future strategies. In summary, OD is highly prevalent and clinically significant in OSA patients, with a complex pathophysiological basis involving multiple interacting factors. Larger-sample, mechanism-driven, and intervention-focused studies are warranted to deepen our understanding of OSA-related OD and to support the development of more precise therapeutic approaches.

paper.title: The Oral Microbiota-Taste Axis: Microbial Influences on Gustatory Perception and Food Sensory Experience.
paper.abstract: Taste is a key determinant of food choice and dietary behavior, yet differences in taste perception are often attributed mainly to genetic variation, taste receptor expression, and neural processing. Emerging evidence suggests that the oral microbiota may represent an additional, and largely overlooked, factor influencing gustatory perception. This review examines the potential role of oral microorganisms in shaping taste by bringing together current evidence from oral microbiology, taste physiology, and nutritional science. Particular attention is given to the close association between tongue-associated microbial communities and taste buds, and to the potential effects of microbial biofilms, local pH changes, and microbial metabolites on the chemical environment surrounding taste receptors. The review further considers how these interactions may influence taste sensitivity, food preferences, dietary patterns, and, ultimately, metabolic health. Importantly, current evidence remains largely associative, and direct mechanistic links between specific microorganisms, microbial metabolites, and taste receptor function are still poorly defined. We therefore highlight key methodological and knowledge gaps and discuss emerging opportunities for dietary modulation, oral probiotics, and microbiome-informed approaches. Understanding this oral microbiota-taste axis may provide a new perspective on taste variability and its nutritional consequences.

paper.title: Remodeling of the olfactory mucosa: maturation of glia, fibroblasts and vascular compartments after birth.
paper.abstract: Despite extensive research on the olfactory epithelium during embryonic and postnatal stages, little is known about peripartum adaptations. Here we describe the profound changes that occur between E18 and P8 - shortly after birth and exposure to air. In the lamina propria, we observed a significant expansion of extracellular space and axon bundles. Olfactory ensheathing cells, the glia cells of the lamina propria, stopped proliferating and upregulate SOX10 after birth. In addition, only after birth did olfactory ensheathing cells express CLDN5 and PECAM1, both of which tighten blood vessels, as well as gap junction communication and potassium transport proteins. Functional Bowman glands emerged only after birth, similar as the layer of horizontal basal cells. Since horizontal basal cells produce extracellular matrix proteins, laminin localization changed after these cells populated the basal epithelium. Interestingly, embryonic mice showed multiple invaginations of blood vessels throughout the olfactory epithelium, which disappear immediately after birth. Our findings reveal that the lamina propria of the olfactory mucosa undergoes profound postnatal maturation, leading to the establishment of a specialized adult tissue architecture.

paper.title: Convergence of sweet and umami in the mammalian taste bud.
paper.abstract: The sense of taste enables animals to identify nutrients and avoid harmful substances. Although the five basic taste qualities-sweet, umami, bitter, sour, and salty-are mediated by distinct molecular receptors, the extent and functional significance of receptor co-expression remain intensely debated. Here, we use in vivo two-photon calcium imaging in mouse taste buds to directly visualize how taste qualities are encoded by taste receptor cells (TRCs) and by innervating gustatory fiber terminals. We find that most TRCs are selectively activated by a single taste quality. However, a significant population of TRCs responds to both sweet and umami stimuli, consistent with extensive sweet-umami double tuning among gustatory ganglion neurons. Moreover, in situ hybridization reveals co-expression of sweet and umami receptors in TRCs from both mouse tongue and human tongue biopsies. Finally, experiments with conditioned taste aversion, a basic form of learned food avoidance, show that sweet and umami taste cross-generalize behaviorally. Together, our findings reveal significant convergence between sweet and umami taste coding both in the tongue and in the peripheral gustatory neurons.

paper.title: Neuroepigenetic programming by the maternal environment. Part B: independent contribution of methylation and hydroxymethylation in the offspring's olfactory bulb following preconceptional weight loss in mice.
paper.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Recent studies indicate that inadequate maternal diet can influence offspring physiology, metabolism and cognitive health, but the impact of the preconception period remains largely unexplored. We previously showed that maternal weight loss prior to conception affects metabolic outcomes and olfactory-driven behaviors in mouse offspring. To explore whether these intergenerational effects are linked to epigenetic mechanisms in the olfactory bulb (OB), we investigated changes in DNA methylation, specifically 5-methylcytosine (5mC) and 5-hydroxymethylcytosine (5hmC), the latter being relatively abundant in the brain but still poorly characterized.

RESULTS: We profiled DNA methylation and hydroxymethylation using Reduced Representation Bisulfite Sequencing (RRBS) and oxidative RRBS (oxRRBS) on OBs from offspring born to control or weight loss mothers, to enable a distinct quantification of 5mC and 5hmC levels at the same CpG sites. While 5mC was globally more abundant in the OB, a subset of CpGs showed high 5hmC levels that varied with maternal condition. Differential analysis identified more differential hydroxymethylated CpG (DhMCs, n = 2631) than differential methylated positions (DMC, n = 1834), indicating a stronger impact of maternal WL on hydroxymethylation. Both DMCs and DhMCs were enriched in genes involved in synaptic function, neuronal signaling, and energy metabolism. However, uniquely modified CpGs, i.e. those detected as modified in only one assay (RRBS or oxRRBS), revealed distinct functional profiles: uniquely differentially hydroxymethylated CpGs (uniqDhMCs) were enriched in genes related to neuronal activity and plasticity, while uniquely differentially methylated CpGs (uniqDMCs) were associated with chromatin remodeling and transcriptional regulation. These findings suggest that, although 5mC and 5hmC can impact similar pathways, they contribute differently to gene regulation in response to early-life nutritional environments.

CONCLUSION: Our study highlights the feasibility of integrating 5mC and 5hmC analyses and uncovers their distinct genomic distributions. The maternal preconceptional weight loss induces lasting and specific epigenetic changes in the OB, notably through 5hmC-specific targeting on genes involved in neuronal activity. By distinguishing between shared and unique DMCs and DhMCs, we reveal complementary and functionally distinct contributions of 5mC and 5hmC to brain plasticity. These findings underscore the importance of integrating both epigenetic marks to fully understand how early-life environmental cues shape neural function and behavior.

paper.title: Masitinib-loaded poly(lactic-co-glycolic acid) nanoparticles reinstate lysosomal acidification and drive immunomodulation in Alzheimer's disease.
paper.abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) poses a formidable therapeutic challenge due to its intricate pathological mechanisms and the blood-brain barrier (BBB). Via transcriptomic analyses and experimental validation, we identify that a malignant neuro-immune pathological cycle, driven by neuronal lysosomal acidification dysfunction and microglial immune activation, potently accelerates AD pathogenesis. Then, we engineer a simple bifunctional intranasal delivery system (PLGA@M) by loading masitinib into poly(lactic-co-glycolic acid) (PLGA) nanoparticles. Following intranasal administration, PLGA@M bypasses the BBB to enter the brain directly via olfactory and trigeminal nerves. PLGA degrades to release acidic moieties, lowering lysosomal pH and restoring autophagic flux, while masitinib inhibits microglial colony stimulating factor 1 receptor signaling, attenuating microglial proliferation, excessive activation and neuroinflammation. Behavioral assays confirm that PLGA@M markedly reverses cognitive deficits in AD mice. This system upgrades PLGA from a mere carrier to a therapeutic component, featuring simplicity, high efficiency and great clinical translation potential.

paper.title: Targeting cyclic-AMP/phosphodiesterase signaling to quiet nasal tuft cell calcium responses.
paper.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Airway tuft cells, also called solitary chemosensory cells, are enriched in nasal polyps and are likely the main epithelial source of interleukin-25 (IL-25) in chronic rhinosinusitis with nasal polyps (CRSwNP). Tuft cells are activated through G protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs) that signal through Ca 2+ . These receptors may also lower cyclic AMP (cAMP), but whether the cAMP pathway can be used to suppress tuft cell responses is unknown.

METHODS: Ca 2+ and cAMP were measured by live cell imaging in isolated Trpm5-GFP mouse nasal tuft cells, and Ca 2+ responses were measured in primary human nasal epithelial air-liquid interface (ALI) cultures from patients with CRSwNP. Defensin and IL-25 release were measured by ELISA and ciliary beat frequency (CBF) by high-speed imaging. Phosphodiesterase (PDE) expression was assessed using publicly available single cell RNA sequencing datasets.

RESULTS: Agonists of bitter taste receptors (T2Rs), the succinate receptor SUCNR1, and the A1 adenosine receptor increased Ca 2+ in GFP-positive mouse nasal tuft cells. T2R and A1 receptor stimulation also lowered cAMP, and these decreases were blocked by pertussis toxin. Glucose, which activates taste family 1 receptors, increased cAMP. Tuft cells were enriched for Pde2a . PDE2A-selective inhibitors (PF-05180999 and BAY 60-7550) increased cAMP and reduced agonist-evoked Ca 2+ responses in mouse tuft cells. In human nasal ALIs, both compounds reduced denatonium-evoked Ca 2+ responses, defensin release, and IL-25 release without increasing CBF.

CONCLUSIONS: GPCRs that activate nasal tuft cells also lower cAMP, and by raising cAMP through PDE2A inhibition, tuft cell Ca 2+ signaling and IL-25 release were reduced in vitro.

paper.title: Intranasal nano-immunotherapy for glioma: bypassing the blood-brain barrier, reprogramming the immune microenvironment, and bridging preclinical validation.
paper.abstract: Glioma, particularly glioblastoma, remains difficult to treat because of limited drug penetration across the blood-brain barrier, profound immune suppression, and insufficient intracranial exposure of systemic immunotherapies. Intranasal nano-immunotherapy is being explored as a potential strategy that may integrate noninvasive nose-to-brain delivery with nanocarrier-mediated immune reprogramming. Intranasal administration may partially bypass conventional vascular barriers through olfactory, trigeminal, mucosal, cerebrospinal-fluid, and perivascular transport routes, while nanoparticles are designed to protect immune-active payloads, support brain tumor targeting, and enable controlled release. Current evidence spans three distinct levels: direct intranasal glioma nano-immunotherapy, intranasal glioma nanodelivery without demonstrated immune reprogramming, and non-intranasal glioma nano-immunotherapy that provides mechanistic support for future intranasal adaptation. Across these evidence levels, investigated platforms include peptide-guided nanomicelles, lipid nanoparticles, biomimetic nanoparticles, ferritin-based nanovectors, spherical nucleic acids, extracellular vesicles, bacterial outer membrane vesicles, and stimuli-responsive systems. These platforms can deliver immune-activating cargos, such as STING or TLR agonists; gene-regulatory cargos, such as siRNA and CRISPR-Cas9 components; and microenvironment-modulating cargos, such as chemokine-axis inhibitors, checkpoint-modulating agents, and combination payloads. Through these payloads, intranasal nanoplatforms may activate innate immune sensing, reverse myeloid-mediated suppression, enhance T-cell infiltration, and induce immunogenic cell death. However, translation remains limited by dosing uncertainty, species differences in nasal anatomy, mucosal and neurological safety concerns, manufacturing complexity, and incomplete immune pharmacodynamic validation. This review summarizes recent advances in intranasal and brain-targeted glioma nano-immunotherapy, highlights key immune mechanisms, and proposes a preclinical validation framework for evaluating whether experimental efficacy can be advanced toward clinically testable treatment designs.

paper.title: Identifying Key Odorant Compounds and Assessing Odor Additivity in Complex Mixtures via Machine Learning: A Multi-Regional Case Study in China.
paper.abstract: With the continuous development of industrial parks in China, odor pollution resulting from the extensive use of solvents has become increasingly prominent, making its accurate analysis and effective prevention and control critically important. To identify key odorant compounds in complex mixtures, this study collected 426 air samples from industrial parks in Guangdong and Zhejiang, China and built a database of odor concentrations and chemical compositions. Machine learning (AutoGluon) combined with SHAP interpretability analysis was employed to build an odor concentration prediction model. The optimal strategy used the Odor Activity Value (OAV) as input for an ExtraTrees model, achieving a pooled out-of-fold R2 of 0.52 under nested cross-validation. Combining SHAP (Shapley additive explanations) interpretability analysis of this optimal model with OAV screening identified 15 key odorant compounds, including methanethiol, tetrachloroethane, acrolein, among others. Further investigation assessed the additivity of odor perception: the summed odor activity value (ΣOAV) failed to reproduce the measured odor concentration, and 81% of the valid samples showed supra-additive behavior. This deviation was closely associated with the analytical coverage of the dominant odorants: sulfur-rich samples were close to additive, whereas sulfur-poor samples deviated by up to two orders of magnitude. The additivity index therefore reflects the completeness of the monitoring list and provides no evidence for or against pairwise sensory interactions. This study validates a data-driven approach for deciphering complex odor formation, providing a powerful methodology for key odorant screening and a scientific foundation for targeted odor pollution control.

paper.title: Small-Pore Chitosan Microcarriers Support Surface-Adherent Growth of Induced Pluripotent Stem Cell-Derived Neural Stem Cells and Improve Intranasal Therapy of Murine Anosmia.
paper.abstract: Intranasal delivery of neural stem cells offers a non-invasive strategy for central nervous system repair, yet its efficacy is limited by rapid mucociliary clearance and poor cellular retention. Although chitosan-based carriers have been explored, the architectural principles governing neural stem cell behavior in the intranasal microenvironment remain poorly defined. We compared chitosan microcarriers (CSMs) with three pore architectures (mean surface pore sizes 4.7 ± 1.7, 15.9 ± 3.2, and 20.5 ± 0.7 µm), fabricated via freezing-controlled phase separation, using induced pluripotent stem cell-derived neural stem cells (iPSC-NSCs). Cellular responses did not vary linearly with pore size: the smallest-pore formulation, CSM-196, supported surface-adhesion-dominant growth, whereas both larger-pore formulations supported infiltration-dominant growth. CSM-196 was also associated with increased proliferative activity, spontaneous neuronal differentiation, and elevated neurotrophic factor secretion without exogenous induction factors. In a methimazole-induced anosmia model, the CSM-196-iPSC-NSC formulation produced greater improvements in olfactory behavioral recovery, olfactory epithelial thickness, neuronal marker expression, and epithelial proliferation than cell-only delivery administered by the same route and schedule. This chitosan-based platform provides a surface-adhesion-oriented cell-delivery strategy that warrants further evaluation for intranasal neural regenerative therapy.

paper.title: Neuropeptidergic-glutamatergic circuit regulates selective forgetting of olfactory learning.
paper.abstract: Forgetting is an active and essential process for adapting to constantly changing environments, yet the molecular and circuit mechanisms underlying selective forgetting remain poorly understood. Our previous studies in the nematode Caenorhabditis elegans suggested that non-cell-autonomous neurosecretory signals accelerate forgetting of olfactory memory for diacetyl, an attractive odorant, by erasing its memory trace, which can be detected as changes in odor-evoked Ca2+ responses in sensory neurons. However, the identity of the forgetting signal, the circuit through which it acts to erase the sensory memory trace, and the time window in which forgetting occurs have remained elusive. Here, we identify a neuropeptidergic-glutamatergic circuit in C. elegans that drives the selective forgetting of olfactory memory. Our genetic and imaging analyses revealed that the gonadotropin-releasing hormone (GnRH)-related neuropeptide NLP-47, secreted from AWC neurons, acts on its receptor GNRR-1 in AIZ interneurons. Glutamatergic neurotransmission from AIZ interneurons then erases the sensory memory trace in AWA neurons via GLR-4, an AMPA-type receptor expressed in AWA. Optogenetic silencing of AWC and AIZ showed that this circuit acts during the recovery phase following conditioning, defining a critical temporal window for active forgetting. This neuropeptidergic-glutamatergic pathway selectively promotes forgetting of a specific odorant memory without affecting another formed simultaneously. Together, our findings demonstrate that neuropeptidergic signaling promotes selective forgetting via a glutamatergic circuit, highlighting that active forgetting is regulated within a critical temporal window and with remarkable specificity.

paper.title: Diffuse mild TBI reveals spatially selective vulnerability from early olfactory disruption to delayed substantia nigra involvement.
paper.abstract: Traumatic brain injury (TBI) is associated with an increased risk of Parkinson's disease (PD), yet the anatomical routes through which diffuse injury confers selective neuronal vulnerability remain poorly defined. The olfactory system occupies a critical peripheral-central interface: primary olfactory neurons project unmyelinated axons through the cribriform plate into the olfactory bulb, rendering this pathway susceptible to mechanical stress while overlapping with one of the earliest sites of α-synuclein pathology in PD. Here, we tested whether diffuse mild TBI produces spatially and temporally distinct neuropathological responses across the olfactory-nigrostriatal axis. Adult C57BL/6 mice underwent mild TBI using the Closed Head Impact Model of Rotational Acceleration and were assessed at 24 h, 1 month, and 6 months post-injury. Holocranioimmunohistochemistry preserving anatomical continuity between the olfactory epithelium (OE) and olfactory bulb enabled integrated analysis of peripheral and central structures. Diffuse injury produced acute axonal disruption of olfactory receptor neurons and was accompanied by transient immune cell accumulation and altered neuronal turnover in the OE. These changes largely resolved by one month, although a modest reduction in mature receptor neurons persisted. In contrast, central olfactory regions demonstrated sustained microglial elevation together with delayed increases in phosphorylated α-synuclein occurring without corresponding changes in total α-synuclein expression. Delayed vulnerability emerged within the substantia nigra, where dopaminergic neuron density was reduced at six months despite preserved striatal terminals. This was accompanied by increased total α-synuclein in the absence of phosphorylation at serine-129, consistent with altered protein handling rather than phosphorylation-dominant aggregation. Together, diffuse mild TBI produced early peripheral disruption followed by persistent region-specific neuroimmune activation and divergent alterations in α-synuclein biology, culminating in delayed nigral susceptibility without evidence of progressive synucleinopathy. These findings identify the olfactory-nigrostriatal axis as a site of trauma-related vulnerability and provide a neuropathological framework linking diffuse injury to processes relevant to later neurodegenerative disease.

paper.title: Olfactory Receptor 51E2 Activation by β-Ionone Induces a Senescence-Like Phenotype and Increases Susceptibility to Senolytic Treatment in Colorectal Cancer.
paper.abstract: Olfactory receptor 51E2 (OR51E2) is markedly downregulated in colorectal cancer (CRC), yet its functional activation by its natural agonist, β-ionone, suppresses CRC cell growth. In this study, we investigated the tumor-suppressive effects of β-ionone-mediated OR51E2 activation using human CRC cell lines (SW480, SW620, and RKO) and patient-derived organoids (PDOs). We demonstrate that β-ionone treatment stimulates intracellular calcium levels in an OR51E2-dependent manner, upregulating MAPK-directed phosphatases (DUSP1/2/4 and PPP1CA). This calcium-dependent phosphatase activation suppresses the MEK1/2-ERK1/2 signaling axis, leading to G0/G1 cell cycle arrest via the downregulation of CDK2/4/6 and cyclin A/D1. Concurrently, OR51E2 activation induces a senescence-like phenotype, evidenced by increased senescence-associated β-galactosidase activity, chromatin remodeling (reduced LAMIN B1 and increased H3K27me3), and upregulated p16/p21 expression alongside senescence-associated secretory phenotype (SASP) factors. These phenotypic and mechanistic findings were fully recapitulated in CRC-PDOs representing distinct clinical subtypes. Crucially, the residual senescence-like cell population showed increased susceptibility to dasatinib plus quercetin (DQ), which reduced senescence-associated markers and increased apoptosis. Collectively, this study demonstrates that OR51E2 activation coordinates a heterogeneous cell-fate decision encompassing both apoptosis and a senescence-like phenotype. Our findings highlight ectopic olfactory receptor signaling as an underexplored mechanism of tumor suppression and provide in vitro evidence for a sequential approach in CRC in which β-ionone-mediated OR51E2 activation induces a senescence-like state followed by senolytic treatment.

paper.title: Enteroendocrine signaling in irritable bowel syndrome: beyond cell counts toward stimulus-responsive physiological profiling.
paper.abstract: Meals are a major symptom trigger in irritable bowel syndrome (IBS), yet the endocrine steps linking luminal nutrients to pain, bloating, urgency, and altered bowel habits remain poorly defined. Early studies relied heavily on mucosal enteroendocrine cell (EEC) counts. Those observations remain informative, particularly in post-infectious IBS, but findings vary with intestinal site, bowel-habit phenotype, staining, and morphometry, and cell abundance does not measure secretory function. Human meal-challenge studies distinguish circulating concentrations from stimulus-evoked responses. In IBS with diarrhea, higher fasting and fed plasma 5-hydroxytryptamine (serotonin, 5-HT) may reflect altered handling more than a uniformly exaggerated postprandial response, whereas IBS with constipation can show impaired stimulus-evoked release. Cholecystokinin, peptide YY, motilin, ghrelin, and related peptides also vary with sex, bowel habit, and visceral sensitivity. Recent human organoid and transcriptomic studies identify distinct nutrient-sensing programs among EEC subtypes and provide a cellular framework for this heterogeneity. We integrate these findings across luminal sensing, secretion, metabolism, receptor responsiveness, and motor or sensory output. The evidence does not support a single IBS endocrine signature. Standardized nutrient challenges linked to serial hormone measurements, mucosal molecular data, and objective physiological readouts are more likely to yield reproducible and clinically testable response patterns.

paper.title: Food perception alone stimulates oviposition through serotonin signaling in Drosophila.
paper.abstract:
UNLABELLED: Reproduction is strongly shaped by nutrient availability, but whether sensory information about food can regulate reproductive output before nutrients are consumed remains unclear. Here, using Drosophila melanogaster , we show that sensory perception of dietary yeast, a protein-rich food source widely used to stimulate fecundity in the fruit fly, is sufficient to rapidly promote egg laying. Specifically, we found that yeast odor exposure increased the rate of oviposition and the number of eggs laid within hours, independent of yeast intake, and that this response was mediated by olfactory signaling through the odorant receptor co-receptor Orco. We further identified serotonin receptor 2A (5-HT2A), but not 5-HT2B, as necessary for yeast odor-induced egg laying. We then asked whether yeast odor also elicits broader life-history changes and whether its reproductive and longevity effects depend on a shared mechanism. Consistent with previous observations, yeast odor also shortened lifespan. However, this lifespan effect was independent of 5-HT2A signaling, indicating that the reproductive and longevity responses to food perception are separable. Finally, our brain connectomic analyses revealed that yeast-responsive olfactory neurons preferentially influence oviposition descending neurons (OviDNs) compared with other olfactory neurons. OviDNs further connect with endocrine-related circuitry in the corpora allata (CA), and, most interestingly, the interneurons linking OviDNs to CA neurons are enriched for serotonergic and dopaminergic modulation. Taken together, our observations indicate that nutrient acquisition is not a prerequisite for animals to adjust their reproduction to the nutritional environment. Sensory information predicting food availability itself can elicit changes in neural state, likely through olfactory-reproductive circuits, that acutely alter reproductive physiology.

SIGNIFICANCE STATEMENT: Food perception can drive changes beyond feeding-related behaviors. This study establishes that olfactory perception of dietary yeast per se elicits egg-laying behavior in Drosophila melanogaster and that the conserved neuromodulator serotonin is required for this response. Our observations suggest that the reproductive state of animals is determined not only by commonly recognized factors such as ingested nutrients, but also by sensory cues that anticipate food availability.

paper.title: Integrated machine learning and in vitro pipeline for TRPA1-active chemesthetic flavor compounds: From predictive screening to molecular mechanisms.
paper.abstract: Chemesthesis constitutes a fundamental dimension of food sensory perception, triggered by transient receptor potential ankyrin 1 (TRPA1) ion channels that mediate responses to pungent and irritating flavor compounds. Here, we developed an integrated computational and in vitro pipeline to overcome this limitation. Using an optimized Random Forest (RF) machine learning model, we successfully predicted and screened representative flavor compounds. We empirically validated these predictions using a newly constructed TRPA1 cell line, where calcium flux assays confirmed dose-dependent channel activation by the selected candidates. Furthermore, molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulations elucidated the activation mechanisms at the atomistic level, identifying key interacting residues. This multidisciplinary framework enables efficient targeted screening of sensory receptor ligands and provides deep molecular insights into flavor-driven chemesthetic perception.

paper.title: The Associations Between Olfactory Bulb Morphology, Volume Change, and Olfactory Recovery.
paper.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To investigate whether olfactory bulb (OB) morphology is associated with olfactory recovery following olfactory training (OT) in individuals with COVID-19-related smell loss.

STUDY DESIGN: Prospective observational study.

SETTING: University hospital and research center.

METHODS: Twenty women with COVID-19-associated olfactory dysfunction and 19 healthy controls underwent OT for 3 months. OB shape (oval vs non-oval) was classified using high-resolution magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), and bilateral OB volumes were manually segmented before and after OT. Olfactory performance was assessed with the Sniffin' Sticks test. Statistical analyses included independent t tests, multimodal analysis of covariance, correlation analyses, and generalized estimating equations.

RESULTS: At baseline, OB volume correlated significantly with olfactory performance. Changes in left OB volume were positively correlated with changes in odor threshold. Following OT, patients with non-oval OB shapes showed greater improvement in Threshold + Discrimination + Identification (TDI) scores and enlargement of left OB volume compared to those with oval-shaped OB. However, OB morphology did not significantly change over time in both patients and controls.

CONCLUSION: OB shape may provide a novel perspective for predicting prognosis after OT. Further studies with larger cohorts and extended training durations are warranted to validate these preliminary observations.

paper.title: Prediction of the binding modes between key differential flavor compounds in tobacco leaves at different maturity stages and the olfactory receptor OR1D2.
paper.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Leaf maturity is a critical determinant of the sensory quality of tobacco. To elucidate the microstructural characteristics of Yunyan 87 tobacco at distinct maturity stages and the perception mechanisms of key differential flavor compounds mediated by the olfactory receptor OR1D2.

METHODS: This study combined scanning electron microscopy (SEM) and untargeted metabolomics with molecular docking and molecular dynamics (MD) simulations to elucidate the binding mechanisms of key flavor compounds to the olfactory receptor OR1D2.

RESULTS: The results indicated that as maturity progressed, the epidermal cell arrangement transitioned from compact to loose, accompanied by an increase in intercellular spaces. Concurrently, the surface microstructure evolved from gentle striations at the unripe stage to distinct ridges or rugae at the mature and overripe stages. Metabolomic analysis revealed that 226 metabolites were identified in both unripe (QS) and mature (GS) leaves, whereas the number increased to 233 in overripe (CS) leaves. A total of 10 differentially abundant metabolites were screened across the three groups. Notably, the contents of key aroma compounds including γ-valerolactone, benzaldehyde, β-cyclocitral, and isopentenol were significantly higher in mature leaves compared to unripe and overripe samples. Molecular docking analysis demonstrated significant variations in binding affinity between the 10 differential flavor compounds and the OR1D2 receptor, with β-cyclocitral exhibiting the strongest binding energy. Molecular dynamics simulation further confirmed the stable binding complex, revealing that the interaction was primarily driven by van der Waals forces, supplemented by electrostatic and hydrophobic interactions.

DISCUSSION: Collectively, these findings indicate that harvesting Yunyan 87 at the mature stage is optimal for maximizing quality. This study provides a theoretical foundation for the precise regulation of harvesting maturity in tobacco production.

paper.title: A Nature-Derived Peptide Promotes Satiety Hormone Response and Weight Loss In Vivo.
paper.abstract: The global rise of obesity highlights the critical need for effective weight-management strategies. GLP-1 receptor agonists have transformed obesity care, yet gastrointestinal intolerance, high cost, and weight regain after discontinuation highlight the need for complementary, orally available options. An alternative is to stimulate the body's own GLP-1 release through the nutrient-sensing GPCRs on enteroendocrine L cells that a meal engages. Using an AI-guided screen of common food proteins, we identified nature-derived peptides (NDPs): sequences native to edible proteins that were reproduced synthetically and engage these receptors. Unlike peptide drugs engineered for systemic exposure, NDPs are intended to act locally at the gut epithelium. Our lead, NDP-35 (from Coffea arabica), is a potent, selective GPR40 agonist (EC50 = 32.7 nM); in mice, it raised plasma GLP-1, GIP, and PYY while lowering hunger hormones, reproducing the coordinated satiety hormone response of a meal at minimal caloric cost. Over 28 days of oral dosing in diet-induced obese rats, NDP-35 reduced food intake and lowered body weight by ∼5%, versus a 3% gain in vehicle-treated animals; a subcutaneous semaglutide arm was included as a reference comparator and endpoint values were of similar magnitude to NDP-35. Terminal clinical chemistry and organ-weight markers showed no treatment-related changes over the dosing period. A structurally distinct peptide, NDP-45 (from banana), reproduced these effects. NDP-35 and NDP-45 are promising preclinical food-protein-derived peptide candidates that stimulate enteroendocrine hormone responses and reduce food intake and body weight in rodent models, warranting further evaluation as an oral approach to appetite and body-weight control.

paper.title: Effects of plant community scenes and odors on thermal perception and physiological responses in a mildly warm environment.

paper.title: Photobiomodulation for radiotherapy-induced dysgeusia in head and neck cancer patients: a pilot randomized clinical trial.

paper.title: Olfactory function in patients with rheumatoid arthritis and its association with disease activity: a cross-sectional case-control study.
paper.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: The aim of this study was to evaluate odor identification and odor threshold in patients with rheumatoid arthritis, compare these measures with those of healthy controls, and investigate their associations with disease activity.

METHODS: This cross-sectional case-control study with prospective participant recruitment included patients with rheumatoid arthritis and age- and sex-matched healthy controls. Odor identification (OI) was assessed using the 12-item Rapid Sniffin' Sticks test, and odor threshold (OT) was assessed using the modified CCCRC n-butanol test. Disease duration, disease activity scores, and inflammatory markers, including C-reactive protein (CRP), were recorded. Associations between olfactory measures and disease-related parameters were analyzed.

RESULTS: The distribution of odor threshold categories differed significantly between groups (p < 0.001), with higher proportions of anosmia and hyposmia in patients with rheumatoid arthritis than in healthy controls. Odor identification scores did not differ significantly between groups. No statistically significant associations were observed between OT categories or OI scores and disease duration, disease activity scores, or CRP levels. OI scores were higher among methotrexate users than non-users, whereas OT category distribution did not differ significantly according to methotrexate use. Neither olfactory measure was significantly associated with corticosteroid use.

CONCLUSION: Rheumatoid arthritis was associated with an altered distribution of odor threshold categories, whereas odor identification scores did not differ significantly between groups. No statistically significant associations were observed between the olfactory measures and disease activity, disease duration, or CRP levels. These findings do not establish causality or independence from potential confounders.

LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: III. Key Points • Patients with rheumatoid arthritis had higher proportions of anosmia and hyposmia than healthy controls. • Odor identification scores did not differ significantly between patients with rheumatoid arthritis and healthy controls. • No statistically significant associations were observed between odor threshold categories or odor identification scores and disease activity, disease duration, or CRP levels. • Rheumatoid arthritis was associated with an altered distribution of odor threshold categories; the independence and causal nature of this association remain to be established.

paper.title: Olfactory Perception Regularities of Structurally Related γ-Lactones: Insights from OR2W1 Selectivity.

paper.title: Shapley fields reveal mosaic chemotopic organization in the mouse Olfactory bulb across diverse chemical feature sets.
paper.abstract: Neural representations in the olfactory bulb (OB) remain poorly understood compared to well-established coding principles in other sensory systems. This difficulty arises because a natural coordinate system for olfactory stimulus space has not yet been identified, complicating the characterization of neural receptive fields analogous to those in other sensory modalities. Moreover, the extent to which these tuning properties are spatially organized within the OB remains unclear. To advance our understanding of the olfactory coding, we introduce an interpretable method of Shapley fields, as an olfactory analog of retinotopic receptive fields. Shapley fields are spatial distributions of chemical feature importance for the tuning of OB glomeruli. We used this tool to investigate chemotopy in the OB with diverse sets of chemical features using widefield epifluorescence recordings of the mouse dorsal OB in response to stimuli across a wide range of the chemical space. This organization was consistent across animals and mostly agreed across very different chemical feature sets: (i) the expert-curated PubChem database features and (ii) features derived from a Graph Neural Network trained on human olfactory perceptual tasks. This chemotopy involved at least three chemical feature dimensions, rather than one or two dominant properties. Moreover, we found that the principal components of the Shapley fields corresponded to single commonly accepted chemical classification groups. This implies that these chemical groups could have been identified purely from the mouse olfactory responses. paper.title: Lower Olfactory Sensitivity in Retronasal Olfaction.
paper.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To directly compare orthonasal and retronasal olfactory function using the recently introduced odorant containers, which enable retronasal stimulation without gustatory or somatosensory involvement.

DESIGN: Experimental study employing a within-subjects design.

SETTING: Laboratory-based olfactory testing facility.

PARTICIPANTS: Thirty-one healthy young adults (19 females; mean age 29.2 years, SD 5.9).

MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: We assessed odour threshold, discrimination and identification with procedures closely adapted from the Sniffin' Sticks test battery, implemented for both routes using odorant containers (instead of Sniffin'Sticks pens). In addition, we obtained global olfactory test scores and odour intensity ratings.

RESULTS: Compared with orthonasal olfaction, retronasal olfaction was associated with significantly higher threshold scores, indicating lower sensitivity. We did not observe any significant differences between orthonasal and retronasal olfaction in odour discrimination or identification. In turn, a combined TDI score was significantly higher for orthonasal than retronasal stimulation. Odours were also rated as more intense when presented orthonasally. Notably, participants identified one odour (fish) with significantly lower accuracy in the retronasal condition.

CONCLUSIONS: Retronasally presented odours are perceived as weaker and less detectable than orthonasal odours, despite similar discrimination and identification capacities. These findings highlight perceptual differences between the two olfactory routes and provide experimental validation for the odorant containers method in retronasal testing.

paper.title: Class-wide sequence, structural, and docking-profile diversity of insect odorant receptors and structural specialization of Orco.
paper.abstract: Insect olfaction is facilitated by a heterotetrameric odorant receptor-odorant receptor co-receptor (OR-Orco) complex. However, extensive sequence divergence and lineage-specific expansion have complicated large-scale comparisons of OR repertoires across insects. Here, we integrated sequence similarity, structural similarity, and molecular docking to analyze ORs from 115 insect species. OR repertoire size was associated with adult diet, larval diet, and habitat, but not with circadian rhythm. We developed a 'trunk-branch' network framework to classify ORs according to sequence and structural similarity and used large-scale molecular docking to derive comparative docking profiles. Despite marked differences in sequence- and structural-community composition, almost all sampled orders contained ORs assigned to all six docking-profile communities. Holometabolous insects showed higher OR sequence-community diversity than non-holometabolous insects, and docking-profile composition differed between extant lineages whose order-level origins predate or postdate the end-Permian mass extinction. Most notably, we identified a highly conserved extracellular β-sheet in Orco that restricts ligand access to the binding pocket and may contribute to its reduced capacity to bind natural odorants. The emergence of Orco represents a key evolutionary transition from homomeric receptors to heteromeric OR-Orco complexes, and our results suggest that this transition may have been accompanied by pronounced specialization of the extracellular domain and binding pocket. Together, these analyses provide a class-wide framework for comparing insect OR diversity and generate testable hypotheses for future experimental and evolutionary studies.

paper.title: Spontaneous neural activity in the developing ant olfactory system.
paper.abstract: Spontaneous neural activity is a pillar of mammalian neurodevelopment. In mammals, developing olfactory sensory neurons (OSNs) show spontaneous activity patterns that depend on the olfactory receptor (OR) they express. This activity is necessary for proper sorting of OSN axons into olfactory bulb glomeruli. This contrasts with the simpler olfactory system of the fruit fly Drosophila melanogaster, where antennal lobe glomeruli form without functional ORs. Compared to Drosophila, ants have a vastly expanded olfactory system and, unlike Drosophila, require functional ORs for proper development. This raises the possibility that ants, like mammals, rely on spontaneous neural activity. To test whether developing ant OSNs are spontaneously active, we performed live calcium imaging in translucent pupae of the clonal raider ant Ooceraea biroi, using a transgenic line expressing the genetically encoded calcium indicator GCaMP6s in OSNs. Developing O. biroi OSNs exhibit spontaneous calcium transients from the earliest stages of glomerulus formation, and features of this activity change over the course of metamorphosis. During early stages, activity is faster, varies widely between cells, and is uncorrelated across the OSN population. By mid-metamorphosis, activity has slowed, with longer calcium events and fewer peaks per cell. As pupae approach eclosion, a new mode appears, with rhythmic, sawtooth-shaped calcium events that synchronously engage OSNs in both antennae. This stage-dependent spontaneous activity suggests that the expanded ant olfactory system may use a developmental logic more akin to mammals than to Drosophila.

paper.title: A disynaptic trigeminal circuit for the transformation and integration of oral chemesthesis in male mice.
paper.abstract: Chemesthesis, encompassing oral sensations such as spiciness and coolness, is an important yet incompletely understood component of mammalian chemical sensing. Unlike taste or olfaction, these sensations are conveyed primarily through trigeminal pathways; however, how modality-specific peripheral signals are processed and transformed along central ascending pathways remains poorly understood. Herein, we delineate the structural and functional organization of an ascending trigeminal-brainstem-parabrachial circuit that mediates oral chemesthetic processing in male mice. Using viral tracing, in vivo calcium imaging, and chemogenetic and optogenetic manipulations, we identify a genetically defined disynaptic glutamatergic pathway (trigeminal ganglion → spinal trigeminal nucleus caudalis → lateral parabrachial nucleus) that is both necessary and sufficient for capsaicin- and menthol-evoked defensive behaviors. Although peripheral TRPV1+ and TRPM8+ neurons retain a degree of modality bias, we observe substantial convergence of spicy and cooling signals within the spinal trigeminal nucleus, followed by sustained and synchronized population activity in vglut2+ neurons of the external lateral parabrachial nucleus. This hierarchical transformation from peripheral segregation to central integration reveals the organizational principle by which distinct chemesthetic modalities are progressively integrated along a trigeminal-mediated ascending pathway, providing a circuit-level framework for understanding how chemical stimuli are processed and coordinated to drive defensive behaviors.

paper.title: Respiratory phase orchestrates human olfactory cortical dynamics.
paper.abstract: Olfaction is fundamental to perception, memory, and emotion, yet the neural basis of human odor processing remains poorly understood. We demonstrate that odor-evoked brain activity is organized by respiratory phase-not absolute time-revealing that natural breathing structures olfactory cortical dynamics. Using simultaneous nasal respiration and electroencephalography recordings in [Formula: see text] participants, we delivered naturalistic odors (peppermint, oregano, and grapefruit) synchronized to individual breathing cycles. Odor presentation elicited respiratory phase-locked event-related spectral perturbations (RPL-ERSPs) in frontal and temporal regions, emerging during the first breath after stimulus onset. The most discriminative neural signatures were theta-band activity during inhalation and alpha-band activity during exhalation, patterns that were obscured in traditional time-locked analyses due to natural variability in breath duration. Leave-one-subject-out cross-validation of RPL-ERSPs achieved reliable odor detection (peppermint: AUC [Formula: see text] 0.79; oregano: AUC [Formula: see text] 0.67; grapefruit: AUC [Formula: see text] 0.62), establishing that phase-locked features generalize across individuals. To connect neural responses to perceptual experience without relying on odor naming-which can be disproportionately impaired in some populations-we quantified odor recognition using free-response descriptions scored with a semantic-similarity approach. Behavioral recognition strength paralleled the neural decoding hierarchy across odors, establishing the perceptual validity of RPL-ERSPs. RPL-ERSPs revealed rapid habituation, with decoding performance declining over repeated presentations, due to selective degradation of the most informative phase-locked features. These findings establish respiratory rhythm as a temporal scaffold for human olfactory cortical processing, positioning RPL-ERSPs as a sensitive, task-free approach for assessing olfactory function. We provide an open-source, respiration-synchronized olfactometer design to enable replication and adoption.

paper.title: Deep learning-based prediction of insect odorant receptor-ligand interactions for behavioral regulator discovery.
paper.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Widespread chemical insecticide use causes resistance and ecological damage, driving need for sustainable pest control via olfaction-based behavioral regulators targeting odorant receptors (ORs). Conventional screening is costly and low-throughput. Deep learning (DL) offers solutions but faces challenges of scarce data, distinct OR-ligand binding properties, and requirements for explainability to guide regulator design.

RESULTS: To explore effective representations of volatile compounds under a limited data setting, we developed three deep learning models based on molecular descriptors (Concat-Desc), molecular graphs (Concat-GNN), and Simplified Molecular Input Line Entry System (SMILES) sequences (Cross-Attn) for OR-ligand interaction prediction. Trained on 4566 experimental pairs from M2iOR database, all DL models outperformed quantitative structure-activity relationship (QSAR) baselines. Concat-Desc and Cross-Attn achieved superior performance (test area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) = 0.891-0.927; accuracy = 0.810-0.843). The explainability modules highlighted model-associated ligand features and protein sequence positions.

CONCLUSION: Molecular descriptors and SMILES are effective for volatile compounds in data-limited scenarios, while graph representations require further optimization. Integrated explainability modules provide testable hypotheses for experimental validation and future design, establishing a computational framework for artificial intelligence (AI)-driven insect chemical ecology. Limitations include data scarcity and limited species coverage that future studies must address. © 2026 Society of Chemical Industry.

paper.title: Diffusion tensor imaging and structural MRI reveal early microstructural injury and progressive atrophy of the olfactory bulb in type 1 diabetic rats.
paper.abstract:
PURPOSE: To determine whether diffusion tensor imaging (DTI) can detect early olfactory bulb microstructural abnormalities in streptozotocin (STZ)-induced type 1 diabetes mellitus (T1DM) rats and to investigate their relationship with structural and histopathological changes.

METHODS: Control and STZ-induced T1DM rats underwent DTI, high-resolution structural MRI and histological examination at 2 and 12 weeks after model induction. Fractional anisotropy (FA), mean diffusivity (MD), axial diffusivity (Da), and radial diffusivity (Dr) were measured in the olfactory nerve layer/glomerular layer/external plexiform layer (ONL/GL/EPL), granule cell layer (GCL), and subependymal zone (SEZ).

RESULTS: Compared to the controls, T1DM rats showed decreased FA and increased MD, Da, and Dr in the ONL/GL/EPL at 2 and 12 weeks after model induction. In the GCL, FA was decreased, whereas Dr was increased. No significant diffusion abnormalities were detected in the SEZ. Ultrastructural examination revealed axolemmal disruption, demyelination, reduced axoplasmic content, and axonal vacuolization in the ONL. Voxel-based morphometry (VBM) demonstrated olfactory bulb atrophy as early as 2 weeks, initially involving the GCL and SEZ, with more extensive and regionally heterogeneous atrophy at 12 weeks. Nissl staining confirmed structural atrophy, and increased caspase-3 immunoreactivity supported apoptosis-related tissue injury. STZ-induced T1DM causes early, layer-specific olfactory bulb microstructural abnormalities and progressive structural atrophy.

CONCLUSION: The differing spatial and temporal distributions of diffusion abnormalities and atrophy suggest that DTI and volumetric MRI capture partially distinct aspects of diabetes-associated olfactory bulb injury. DTI may provide a sensitive, noninvasive approach for detecting early microstructural abnormalities before widespread structural loss develops.

paper.title: Odor representations are structured by heterogeneous tuning and concentration-dependence of functionally distinct olfactory sensory neuron subpopulations.
paper.abstract: Olfactory stimuli (odorants) are represented by combinatorial patterns of olfactory sensory neuron (OSN) activation that are translated into spatially-organized glomerular maps at their input to the CNS. How glomerular maps relate to odorant features - including chemical structure and concentration - remains a key question in understanding the neural mechanisms of odor coding. Here, we compared glomerular response maps for the same 59 odorants across three concentration regimes, using GCaMP6 imaging from OSN axon terminals in the olfactory bulb (OB) of the anesthetized mouse. At the lowest regime, in which concentrations were chosen to distinguish the most sensitive glomeruli for each odorant, glomeruli were exceptionally narrowly tuned and responses across glomeruli were extremely sparse. We then compared responses at two higher-concentration regimes, 'low' and 'high', differing by 25-fold from each other and 2 - 5 log units higher than the 'most-sensitive' regime. Increasing concentration broadened tuning of OSN inputs; this broadening was heterogeneous across chemical space and was well-described by classifying glomeruli into several subpopulations with distinct consensus tuning profiles. Each subpopulation was selectively tuned to one or a few odorant chemical classes and spatially clustered in a manner consistent with the projection patterns of receptor-defined OSN classes. Glomerular subpopulations retained distinct tuning and spatial localization even at the highest concentrations. OSN subpopulations thus sample chemical space nonuniformly across a large concentration range. These results suggest a lower-dimensional structure in the representation of odorant information that largely reflects OSN subpopulations which, in turn, map to olfactory receptor subfamilies. This organization may enable distinct odor coding strategies for different OSN classes and for parts of chemical feature space with distinct ethological relevance.

paper.title: Somatotopic Organization of Sensory Inputs From Taste Appendages in the Subesophageal Zone and Brain of the Honey Bee Apis mellifera.
paper.abstract: The study of gustatory pathways from the periphery to the brain offers valuable insights into the neural mechanisms underlying taste processing and foraging choices, particularly in ecologically and economically relevant species such as the honey bee, Apis mellifera. Using anterograde mass staining with dextran-coupled fluorescent tracers applied into the main gustatory appendages (antennae, mouthparts, and foreleg tarsi), we identified the projection areas of their sensory afferents within the SEZ. Our results show that sensory circuits are confined to specific, distinct regions of the SEZ, suggesting the presence of somatotopic "maps" corresponding to the different appendages. We also confirm the subesophageal-calycal tract (SCT) as the main output of the SEZ. Combined retrograde staining of the SCT and anterograde staining of taste appendages revealed that SCT dendrites overlap specifically with sensory input from the maxillae in the SEZ. The functional significance of these findings is discussed in the context of gustatory information processing during bee feeding behavior, and the results are considered within a comparative framework across insect taxa.

paper.title: A multilevel circuit gating framework for transforming sexual motivation into sexual action: Insights from mouse models.
paper.abstract: Sexual behaviour consists of a appetitive phase and a consummatory phase. Based primarily on research evidence from rodents (particularly male mice), this paper presents a multi-level gate model that explains how the transition between these two phases occurs. In this model, the processing of cues associated with a potential mate is initiated in the main olfactory bulb (MOB) and the accessory olfactory bulb (AOB) systems. These cues are then transmitted through limbic circuits, such as the medial amygdala (MeA) and the bed nucleus of the stria terminalis (BNST), where they are encoded as valuable mating information. Subsequently, these cues are integrated with internal motivational states, including social cues, hormonal status, Sexual reward experience, and sexual satiety, within cell-type-specific circuits centred on the preoptic area (POA). This integration process results in the generation of a motivational gain. When intrinsic motivational states are integrated with somatosensory inputs related to the partner, a state-dependent sensory contact gating mechanism facilitates the transition from exploratory contact to mating behaviours (e.g. mounting). In the downstream process, theperiaqueductal gray (PAG), brainstem, spinal cord, and mesolimbic reward circuits coordinate the sequence of intromission and ejaculation behaviours. During the process of mating, feedback mechanisms such as reward reinforcement and sexual reward modulate future motivational states and action thresholds. Finally, we discuss sex differences in the neural mechanisms underlying the transition from appetitive to consummatory. This conceptual model provides a testable hypothesis regarding the neural mechanisms underlying sexual dysfunction caused by insufficient sexual motivation or disrupted action gating thresholds.

paper.title: [Multimodal biomarkers of Parkinson's disease risk in essential tremor. (A prospective cohort study)].
paper.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To identify clinical and neuroimaging biomarkers associated with Parkinson's disease (PD) onset in patients with essential tremor plus (ET-plus) during prospective observation.

MATERIAL AND METHODS: This prospective observational cohort study included 159 patients diagnosed with essential tremor (ET), ET-plus, ET-PD, and idiopathic PD. The median observation period was 4.6 years. All participants underwent standardized neurological examinations and assessments, including the Unified Parkinson's Disease Rating Scale Part III (UPDRS-III), Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA), Scale for the Assessment and Rating of Ataxia (SARA), Unified Dystonia Rating Scale (UDRS), Fahn-Tolosa-Marin Tremor Rating Scale, Non-Motor Symptoms Scale (NMSS), olfactory testing, screening for probable REM sleep behavior disorder (RBD), Stroop test, forward and backward counting tests, Boston Naming Test, literal and semantic verbal fluency tests, transcranial sonography (TCS) of the substantia nigra, and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) with nigrosome-1 assessment.

RESULTS: Conversion from ET-plus to PD occurred in 15 patients. The most significant predictors of conversion were hyperechogenicity of the substantia nigra on transcranial Doppler (TCD), absence of nigrosome-1 on MRI, probable REM sleep behavior disorder (RBD), and ET duration greater than 20 years. The predictive model demonstrated high discriminatory power (C-statistic 0.89). Clinically, patients who converted showed a combination of non-motor symptoms, cognitive decline, signs of nigrostriatal dysfunction, and more frequent resting tremor.

CONCLUSIONS: The risk of Parkinson's disease onset in patients with ET-plus is determined by a combination of multimodal biomarkers. The prospective identification of 15 patients who converted supports classifying this subgroup as a high-risk phenotype that warrants ongoing monitoring and comprehensive evaluation.

paper.title: Full title: From neural excitability to volatile signatures: A mechanistic hypothesis for pre-ictal volatile organic compound signatures in epilepsy.
paper.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Seizure unpredictability remains a major contributor to morbidity in epilepsy, and biomarkers capable of identifying pre-ictal states are critically needed. Volatile organic compounds (VOCs) have emerged as potential noninvasive indicators of seizure susceptibility, yet the biological mechanisms linking pre-ictal neural states to peripheral volatile signatures remain poorly understood.

METHODS: We conducted a narrative review in accordance with the Scale for the Assessment of Narrative Review Articles (SANRA) criteria integrating evidence from epilepsy neurobiology, oxidative stress, autonomic physiology, volatilomics, and seizure-detection science to develop a mechanistic hypothesis linking pre-ictal physiological processes to seizure-associated volatile signatures.

RESULTS: Evidence supports several components of the proposed mechanistic hypothesis, although the strength and directness of evidence vary across pathway components. Pre-ictal states have been associated with increased neuronal excitability, altered neurophysiology, and heightened metabolic demand, creating conditions favorable for oxidative stress. Lipid peroxidation generates volatile and semi-volatile metabolites that can enter systemic circulation and become detectable peripherally. Autonomic modulation may further influence their expression and detectability. Human olfactory and analytical studies provide preliminary evidence for seizure-associated and pre-ictal volatile signatures. Although the complete pathway has not been experimentally validated, available evidence is consistent with a biologically plausible hypothesis linking central physiological processes to peripheral volatile signals.

SIGNIFICANCE: This review proposes a multilevel mechanistic hypothesis for seizure-associated volatile signature generation. Volatile signatures are conceptualized as downstream reflections of physiological states associated with seizure susceptibility. This framework provides a foundation for future investigation of VOC-based seizure forecasting approaches in epilepsy.
